# MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3 Calibration checks - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Scope
- This procedure defines calibration checks and verification activities required on Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). It covers the functional checks that must be performed prior to production after maintenance, after control system changes, or when drift is suspected. The objective is to confirm that measurement, timing, and control elements that affect quench timing and atmosphere control are within acceptable performance prior to processing parts.
- This document applies to maintenance and quality personnel responsible for furnace readiness and calibration verification. Refer to related change notices and equipment manuals for installation and design assumptions: ECN-2026-017, MM-P3-L2-HT03, SB-1041.

Background and rationale
- Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) uses a controlled quench event that must occur within a verified timing window to achieve metallurgical targets. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds. This limit is a control parameter for acceptable furnace-to-quench actuator response and is critical to maintain heat treat consistency.
- Calibration checks focus on sensors, timing relays, control logic, and associated actuators whose performance influences the quench timing and atmosphere control. Ensuring these instruments are within tolerance reduces variability in part hardness and microstructure.
- Where lubrication of actuators or mechanical linkages is required during calibration checks, use the approved lubricant identified for this equipment. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is CFW-LUB-159.

Tools
- Calibration test instrument capable of recording event timing and trigger response as required for furnace control verification. Instrument must be appropriate for the signal types present on EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
- Hand tools and mechanical access equipment as required to access sensors and actuators.
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-159.
- Calibration records and forms per MM-P3-L2-HT03 and SB-1041.
- Lockout/tagout and machine isolation devices per plant procedures referenced in ECN-2026-017.

Procedure
- Prepare: Verify that the furnace is in a safe status for test activities following lockout/tagout procedures. Confirm that the control system is in a diagnostic mode that allows simulated cycles without introducing production parts to process.
- Sensor verification: Inspect signal cables and connectors to ensure secure connections and no visible damage. Exercise each sensor by simulating the condition it detects and observe the control input. Record the observed response timing using the calibration test instrument. The purpose is to detect sensor delays or intermittent signals that could add latency to the quench event.
- Timing path trace: Trace the control path from sensor input through control logic to the quench actuator. Use the calibration test instrument to capture timestamps at key points: sensor out, controller output, and actuator actuation. The rationale is to isolate which element contributes most to total delay and to provide evidence when adjustments or repairs are needed.
- Actuator check and lubrication: Verify mechanical freedom of motion for the quench actuator and linkage. If friction or stiffness is observed, apply the approved lubricant part number CFW-LUB-159 to the specified lubrication points. Operate the actuator through its cycle and measure response time to confirm improvement. Record before-and-after timing values to demonstrate effectiveness.
- Control logic verification: Place the control system into a test mode that permits single-step or simulated events. Command a simulated quench event and capture the elapsed time from command issuance to physical actuator response. Compare the measured elapsed time to the allowable maximum. The purpose is to verify that logic sequencing and communications do not introduce excess delay.
- Repeatability checks: Perform multiple simulated quench events to assess repeatability of response timing. The intent is to identify intermittent delays that could be masked by a single successful test.
- Post-test restoration: Return control system to normal operating mode, remove test instrumentation, and re-secure any access points opened for testing. Ensure lubrication points are properly cleaned and excess lubricant removed.

Acceptance criteria
- Timing performance: The measured total elapsed time from control command to physical quench actuation must be at or below the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03), which is 13 seconds. Any measurement that exceeds this value constitutes a fail and requires troubleshooting per MM-P3-L2-HT03 and ECN-2026-017.
- Sensor and actuator function: Sensors must produce a clean, repeatable signal that triggers control logic without intermittent dropout. Actuators must operate smoothly after any required lubrication with CFW-LUB-159 and must return to their rest positions reliably.
- Repeatability: Timing variability between simulated events should be consistent with historical performance documented in maintenance records; large unexplained variation requires corrective action and root cause analysis as described in ECN-2026-017.

Examples and troubleshooting guidance
- Example scenario: If the measured elapsed time exceeds 13 seconds, capture timestamps at each node in the control path to localize the delay source. Typical findings may include slow sensor response due to contamination, delayed controller output due to queued logic, or mechanical binding in the actuator linkage. Use the recorded timestamps to determine the corrective action scope—electrical, software, or mechanical.
- Use this evidence to support any changes or part replacements and document per ECN-2026-017 and SB-1041. If lubrication reduced timing but timing remains above the limit, escalate to control specialist for logic and I/O verification.

Records to keep
- Completed calibration check form per MM-P3-L2-HT03. Include raw timestamp logs from the calibration test instrument and annotated traces showing the timing path.
- Lubrication log entries when CFW-LUB-159 is applied, including location and maintenance technician identification.
- Nonconformance reports and corrective action records if measured timing exceeds the acceptance criteria, with reference to ECN-2026-017 for change control.
- Retain records in the equipment maintenance file and submit copies to quality per SB-1041.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-017
- MM-P3-L2-HT03
- SB-1041
